title: NbO2 Mott-switch sense latch replaces cross-coupled sense amplifier
idea: Effect: Mott insulator-to-metal transition. Bias a ~20 nm NbO2 threshold switch just below its transition voltage between the bitline and a reference; the cell's ~60 mV charge-sharing signal tips it across threshold, its resistance collapses ~100x in <1 ns, and one restore FET writes the row back. One BEOL device plus 1-2 FETs replaces the 6-10 transistor latch and equalizer.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): sense-amp stripes are ~15-20% of die; a 3-4x smaller SA, which could also sit in BEOL above the array, frees ~10% of die area.

title: Room-temperature Coulomb-blockade electrometer reads half-femtofarad cells
idea: Effect: Coulomb blockade. Put one single-electron transistor with a sub-2 nm Si or metal-nanocluster island (charging energy >10 kT) at each local bitline as an electrometer; its drain current swings full scale for a gate-charge change of e/2, so a storage capacitor 10x smaller (~0.5 fF) still gives a readable swing that then drives a conventional latch.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 10x less Cs lets pillar aspect ratio fall from ~70:1 to ~10:1, removing the hardest etch and deposition steps.

title: Clocked resonant-tunneling-diode pair as monostable-bistable bitline sense element
idea: Effect: resonant tunneling and negative differential resistance. Two series RTDs (Si/SiGe interband or InGaAs/AlAs) form a MOBILE: ramping the clock bias moves the pair from monostable to bistable, and the bitline current imbalance on the middle node decides which RTD drops into its valley. NDR gives regenerative gain with 2 devices at ~0.3 V.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10) and SA area (fact 7): sensing at 0.3-0.5 V cuts SA-stripe CV^2 ~4x, using 2 devices instead of ~8.

title: Magnetoelectric laminates harvest broadcast field to generate wordline boost voltage
idea: Effect: magnetostriction coupled to piezoelectricity. A package-level planar coil broadcasts a ~10 MHz AC magnetic field; each bank carries a FeGa (magnetostrictive) / AlScN (piezoelectric) laminate whose strain produces several volts locally, which a rectifier stores as VPP. This replaces the area-hungry switched-capacitor charge pumps and long VPP buses.
why: Periphery area/energy (facts 7, 10): VPP pumps take ~3-5% of die at ~30% efficiency; local magnetoelectric generation removes pump area and roughly halves VPP distribution loss.

title: Pyroelectric HZO film senses per-mat heating for mat-level refresh scaling
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. Deposit a 10 nm Si-doped HfO2 pyroelectric capacitor (same ALD as HZO) beside each mat; temperature change yields charge dQ = p*A*dT with no bias power, integrated by a shared ADC and periodically re-zeroed against one diode sensor. Refresh rate is then set per mat instead of by the hottest on-die sensor.
why: Refresh (fact 3): retention roughly doubles per ~10 C, so mats 10-15 C cooler than the hotspot can refresh 2-3x less often, cutting refresh energy ~30-40% on unevenly heated dies.

title: Acoustic-resonator frequency-division addressing replaces global predecoder buses
idea: Effect: mechanical (BAW/contour-mode) resonance. Give each subarray block an AlScN resonator tuned to a unique frequency (e.g., 64 tones from 1.0-2.6 GHz); the controller sends a tone burst on one shared line, and only the block whose resonator rings up past threshold enables its local wordline drivers. The address travels as a frequency instead of over dozens of routed wires.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): one RF line can replace ~20-40 global address/predecode wires and repeaters per bank.

title: Band-to-band tunneling FET sense amplifier enables 0.4 V array voltage
idea: Effect: band-to-band (Zener) tunneling. Build the SA cross-coupled pair from vertical Ge/Si heterojunction TFETs with ~30 mV/dec turn-on, so the latch regenerates with only 0.4 V across it; complementary n/p TFET pairs handle their one-way conduction.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): VARY falls from ~1 V to 0.4 V, so bitline CV^2 energy drops ~6x for activation and refresh.

title: Spin-Hall nonvolatile shadow latches let periphery power-gate between accesses
idea: Effect: spin Hall effect (spin-orbit torque). Pair each sense amp with a three-terminal SOT-MTJ on a beta-Ta strip (no tungsten) that copies the latched row in ~1 ns; idle banks cut power to SA and periphery stripes and reopen the row from the shadow copy without a new activation.
why: Idle power and row hammer (fact 9): periphery leakage in idle banks drops ~50-80%, and fewer re-activations lower hammer exposure.

title: Ionic drift leaky-integrator per row counts activations for row hammer
idea: Effect: ion migration. Add a sub-50 nm Ag/SiO2 (or Cu/Ta2O5) ionic cell per row, fed by a small tap from the wordline driver; each ACT pulse pushes a fixed ion dose forward while back-diffusion relaxes it with a ~32-64 ms time constant. Conductance thus encodes activations within the refresh window, and crossing a threshold flags the row for neighbor refresh.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): one BEOL device per row replaces SRAM/CAM counter tables of tens of KB per bank, and the natural decay matches the refresh window at no cost.

title: Electrochromic BIST pads let cameras read wafer test without probe cards
idea: Effect: electrochromism. Each die's built-in self-test drives a small WO3 electrochromic pad (H+ or Li+ intercalation) that turns dark blue when a mat or bank fails. A full-wafer membrane supplies only power and a few control pins, and a camera reads the pass/fail map of every die on the wafer in seconds, so no dense signal probe cards or tester channels are needed.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4): test equipment (testers, probe cards, long retention tests) is ~10-15% of cost; massively parallel optical readout could cut tester capex several-fold.

title: Phase-change repair registers replace laser-fuse banks and their latches
idea: Effect: thermal hysteresis of the amorphous/crystalline phase change. Store redundancy repair addresses in small GST or Sb2Te3-superlattice cells in BEOL, programmed once at test by an on-die micro-heater pulse and read directly by the decoder compare logic. This eliminates pitch-limited laser-fuse banks and the boot-time fuse broadcast latches.
why: Periphery area (fact 7) and capital: ~2-3% of die area recovered and the laser-repair tool step removed.

title: Ferroelectric negative-capacitance layer cancels bitline parasitic capacitance
idea: Effect: ferroelectric negative capacitance. Hang a stabilized HZO/dielectric NC capacitor in parallel on each bitline sense node, tuned so the net node capacitance stays positive but drops ~2x. The charge-transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+CBL) roughly doubles.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): halves the Cs needed (AR ~70:1 to ~40:1), or doubles cells per bitline so half the SA stripes are needed.

title: MOS-varactor capacitance collapse amplifies bitline signal before latching
idea: Effect: parametric amplification (voltage-dependent capacitance). After charge sharing, drive the bottom plate of an accumulation-mode MOS varactor on each bitline into depletion so bitline capacitance falls ~3x; charge is conserved, so the differential voltage grows ~3x (V=Q/C) with no DC current before the latch fires.
why: Sense margin (facts 1, 7): ~3x signal allows 2x longer bitlines (half as many SA stripes) or ~2x smaller Cs.

title: Avalanche-multiplying sense junction gives charge gain before latch
idea: Effect: impact-ionization avalanche multiplication. Transfer cell charge into a small guard-ringed n+/p junction biased just below breakdown in linear mode; injected carriers are multiplied ~10-30x, then the packet is quenched and integrated on the SA node, so gain comes before any transistor offset.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~10x charge gain would allow ~0.5-1 fF cells and faster sensing.

title: Vacuum nanogap field-emission triodes as BEOL wordline drivers
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim field emission in vacuum. Etch sealed ~50 nm vacuum cavities in BEOL with sharp Mo or TiN emitters (no tungsten); grid-gated emission switches ~3 V wordlines with no channel leakage and no thick-oxide HV transistors, stacking the driver bank above the array.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): HV sub-wordline driver strips are ~10% of die; moving them into BEOL could shrink the die ~8%.

title: Electrostatic NEMS relays build zero-leakage row decoders above the array
idea: Effect: electrostatic pull-in hysteresis. Build BEOL TiN or poly-SiGe nano-relays (pull-in ~1-2 V) arranged as a relay-tree row decoder; hysteresis holds the selected path with no static current, and the metal contacts pass the 3 V wordline level directly, so no level shifters are needed.
why: Periphery area/leakage (fact 7): decoder and level-shifter area moves to BEOL and off-state leakage is zero in standby.

title: Ovonic-threshold-switch crosspoint replaces per-row wordline driver selection
idea: Effect: ovonic threshold switching. Select wordlines through a BEOL crosspoint of OTS devices: a group line at +V/2 and an index line at -V/2 exceed the OTS threshold (~1.5 V) only at their intersection, which snaps on and charges that wordline. This is coincident selection, as in core memory, done with threshold switching; N drivers become ~2*sqrt(N).
why: Periphery area (fact 7): ~16x fewer driver transistors per sub-wordline strip for 1024 rows.

title: Hot-carrier-injection trimming nulls sense-amp offset permanently at test
idea: Effect: hot-carrier charge trapping. At wafer test, a built-in ramp measures each SA's offset, then short high-Vds pulses inject hot carriers into the stronger transistor's gate oxide to raise its Vt until the pair balances within ~3 mV; the trapped charge holds for years, with an optional field top-up.
why: SA area (fact 7): offset sets SA sizing (Pelgrom), so cutting sigma from ~15 mV to ~3 mV allows ~4-10x smaller SA devices or 2x cells per bitline.

title: Image-sensor floating-diffusion readout replaces charge sharing with full transfer
idea: Effect: complete charge transfer onto a tiny node (the CMOS image-sensor 4T pixel principle). Every 16 cells share a ~0.3 fF floating diffusion behind a transfer gate and a one-transistor source follower; the cell charge is dumped fully onto the tiny node instead of being shared with a ~50 fF bitline. The follower drives the bitline as a voltage, and correlated double sampling removes kTC reset noise.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): signal per electron rises ~30x, so Cs could drop to ~1 fF (AR ~15:1), removing high-AR capacitor steps.

title: CCD bucket-brigade shifts bitline charges to one shared correlated-double-sampling amplifier
idea: Effect: charge-coupled transfer. Turn local bitlines into buried-channel CCD registers: on activation, cell charges are clocked across 64 columns into a single low-noise floating-diffusion amplifier with correlated double sampling (scientific CCDs reach <5 e- noise), and written back by a reverse shift. One amplifier serves 64 bitlines and resolves ~100-electron packets.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and capacitor wall (fact 1): ~64x fewer sense amps and Cs up to ~20x smaller; the cost is ~32 ns of serial shift latency, which suits burst page fetches.

title: Micro-ring modulators driven directly from sense-amp row skip SerDes
idea: Effect: electro-optic refractive-index modulation (Pockels in thin-film LiNbO3, or carrier plasma dispersion in Si). Put micro-ring modulators at the column-select outputs so each sense-amp group modulates its own WDM wavelength; light carries the page off-die in parallel, eliminating the serializer, DLL and long global data lines.
why: Data movement (fact 5) and periphery (fact 7): I/O energy falls from 3-20 pJ/bit to <1 pJ/bit, and ~10% of die area (I/O plus DLL) is removed.

title: Wavelength-addressed photoconductive switches replace electrical row decoders
idea: Effect: photoconductivity. Run a BEOL SiN waveguide past each sub-wordline driver group, where a ring filter tuned to one of ~64 WDM wavelengths feeds a Ge or a-Si photoconductor that gates the driver; the controller picks a row block by injecting that wavelength, so address decoding happens in the waveguide instead of in CMOS decoder trees.
why: Periphery area/energy (fact 7): removes predecoders and global address wires; photoconductive turn-on is <100 ps.

title: Injection-locked oscillator pair turns bitline signal into phase decision
idea: Effect: sub-harmonic injection locking. Each SA stripe hosts a pair of tiny coupled ring oscillators pumped at their second harmonic, so they become phase-bistable (0 or 180 degrees, as in oscillator Ising machines); the bitline differential briefly biases the coupling, the pair locks into one phase, and a phase detector restores full swing. Gain comes from locking dynamics rather than transistor matching.
why: SA offset and area (facts 7, 10): a phase decision averages mismatch over many cycles, tolerating ~5x worse device matching and working near 0.5 V.

title: Cold-grade bin: immersion racks run retention-reject DRAM dies
idea: Effect: Arrhenius thermally activated junction leakage (~0.6 eV). A 10-person firm buys dies that fail the 85 C/64 ms retention test at scrap prices, has an OSAT package them, and deploys them only in single-phase immersion racks held at 30-40 C, where retention is ~8-16x longer and the dies pass with margin. An off-the-shelf FPGA/CXL controller checks retention at operating temperature.
why: Usable supply: reject bins (an estimated 2-5% of output) become sellable memory with zero fab capex.

title: tRCD-sweep charge spectroscopy predicts per-row retention in seconds
idea: Effect: RC kinetics of charge sharing. A small team's FPGA DDR5 controller reads each row repeatedly while shortening tRCD in 0.5 ns steps; the step where bits flip shows how far the stored charge sits from the sense trip point after a known wait. Fitting the decay gives each row's leakage rate without hour-long pauses, and rows are binned into 64/128/256/512 ms refresh classes.
why: Refresh (fact 3): multi-rate refresh can cut refresh operations ~60-75%, and profiling drops from hours to seconds per DIMM, so it can run in the field.

title: Backside 1064 nm illumination accelerates DRAM retention screening
idea: Effect: photoconductive carrier generation. A benchtop station floods bare dies (or windowed package backs) with calibrated 1064 nm light, which passes through silicon and adds a uniform, dose-set generation current to every storage junction. A known added leakage turns a long retention wait into minutes, and the dose-response slope separates leaky cells from merely marginal ones.
why: Test capital/time (fact 4): 5-10x shorter retention screens cut tester capex per bit and enable fine retention binning for low-refresh SKUs; one optics bench plus an existing tester.

title: Lateral-BJT sense amplifier on open 130 nm PDK gain-cell macro
idea: Effect: Boltzmann-diffusion matching of bipolar Vbe. A small team designs a gain-cell memory macro on a SkyWater/GF open-PDK MPW whose sense amp is a differential pair of parasitic vertical/lateral BJTs. Vbe mismatch is ~0.5-1 mV versus ~10-20 mV for small MOSFETs, so tiny 2T/3T gain-cell read currents are resolved by a small, untrimmed stage.
why: Sense margin and U.S. manufacturability: 512+ cells per SA and lower read currents (longer retention) in a U.S. 130 nm fab, designed fabless.

title: FD-SOI back-gate voltages null sense-amp offset on a 22FDX shuttle
idea: Effect: body effect through the buried oxide. On an FD-SOI MPW, each SA pair's back gate is tied to a small hold capacitor that an auto-zero loop charges during a calibration slot; the ~80 mV/V body coefficient nulls offset and re-calibrates every refresh period, tracking aging and temperature.
why: SA area (fact 7): minimum-size SA devices (4-8x smaller) become usable; GF 22FDX in New York gives a U.S. path for a fabless team.

title: Capacitive self-bootstrap wordlines eliminate the VPP charge pump
idea: Effect: capacitive bootstrap coupling. Revive the NMOS-era trick: the selected wordline driver's gate node is isolated, then kicked by its own rising output through gate-channel capacitance plus a small MOS cap, lifting the wordline to ~2xVDD for the access with no global VPP pump. Proven by a small team on a mature-node MPW macro.
why: Periphery area/energy (facts 7, 10): removes the VPP pump (~3-5% of die, ~30% efficient) and its grid, cutting activation energy ~20%.

title: Latch resolution-time monitor flags weakening cells before they fail
idea: Effect: exponential regeneration in a bistable latch (metastability). Standard-cell time-to-digital counters on a few sense amps per mat measure how long each latch takes to resolve; since resolution time grows as tau*ln(Vswing/dV), a slow decision reveals a cell whose charge is nearing the trip point, and the controller raises refresh only for that row.
why: Refresh (fact 3): sensed per-row margins replace worst-case refresh (~50% fewer refreshes) and catch variable-retention drift online; MPW-buildable.

title: Triple-row charge sharing detects duplicate pages for in-DRAM dedup
idea: Effect: multi-row charge-sharing majority. On commodity DDR4/DDR5, an FPGA controller issues back-to-back ACTs (the timing-violation trick from ComputeDRAM) to open a candidate page, a complement copy of the suspected twin and an all-zero reference together; the result equals the reference wherever the pages agree. Duplicate 8 KB rows are found at sense-amp bandwidth and mapped to one physical copy.
why: Usable supply: VM and AI-serving memory often holds 10-30% duplicate pages (zero pages, shared weights, KV prefixes); cheap in-DRAM comparison enables continuous dedup worth ~+10-25% effective capacity.

title: Paraffin latent-heat buffer keeps DIMMs below the 2x refresh threshold
idea: Effect: latent heat and melt/freeze thermal hysteresis. Bond an encapsulated paraffin/graphite phase-change pad (melting ~75-80 C, ~200 J/g) between DRAM packages and the heat spreader; during load spikes it clamps die temperature below 85 C so the controller never enters JEDEC 2x refresh, and it re-solidifies in lulls.
why: Refresh bandwidth/energy (fact 3): ~10-20% bandwidth recovered on hot servers; off-the-shelf materials and a small hardware team.

title: Leakage-replica decay timer sets refresh interval automatically
idea: Effect: junction/GIDL leakage tracking in replica cells. Each mat holds a few replica storage cells with ~4x smaller capacitance, charged at every refresh and watched by a comparator; because they leak through the same physics as data cells, their threshold crossing marks a self-timed refresh deadline that follows process, voltage and temperature.
why: Refresh (fact 3): typical dies can refresh ~2-4x less often than the fixed worst-case spec; fits a small team's gain-cell/eDRAM macro on MPW.

title: Storage-node-controlled ring-oscillator readout stores two bits per gain cell
idea: Effect: voltage-controlled oscillation frequency. In a 2T gain cell, the storage node gates the current source of a short current-starved ring oscillator shared per column group; a read counts oscillations for ~10 ns, so four charge levels map to clearly separated counts. The count is digital and immune to bitline offset.
why: Density/cost per bit: 2 bits per cell doubles gain-cell macro density on mature U.S. nodes, and counters replace analog SAs; MPW-feasible.

title: LC-resonant adiabatic driver chiplet recycles command/address bus energy
idea: Effect: LC resonance energy recovery. A small mature-node chiplet drives the DRAM command/address and clock nets as part of an LC tank (on-package inductor plus net capacitance), so energy sloshes between the inductor and the wires instead of being dumped as CV^2 on every toggle; commands are encoded by pulse position on the resonant waveform.
why: Data-movement/periphery energy (fact 5): CA and clock bus energy cut ~60-75%; MPW plus OSAT only.

title: Mandate hammer-threshold grading so retired DIMMs re-enter service
idea: Effect: wordline-coupling disturbance (row-hammer first-flip count, HCfirst). Policy plus small lab: before hyperscaler DIMMs are shredded, a standard FPGA test measures each module's HCfirst and retention spread; modules get grades (e.g., hammer-tolerant, read-mostly cache tier) under an OCP spec and are resold, with reuse tax credits.
why: Usable supply: datacenters retire DRAM after 4-6 years while most cells are healthy; recovering 20% of retired DDR4/DDR5 adds supply with zero fab capex.

title: Piezo-stack package clamp tunes die stress to shrink leakage tail
idea: Effect: piezo-junction effect (stress-modified bandgap and trap emission rates). A small mechanical team builds a module heat spreader with a PZT stack that applies controlled compressive stress (tens of MPa) to DRAM packages; a closed loop driven by measured retention finds the stress setpoint that minimizes trap-assisted junction leakage.
why: Refresh (fact 3): if the leakage tail shrinks 1.5-2x, the refresh interval stretches by the same factor with no die change.

title: Photoconductive-switch probe card multiplexes thousands of test channels optically
idea: Effect: picosecond photoconductive switching in low-temperature-grown GaAs. Build DRAM wafer probe cards whose fan-out uses LT-GaAs photoconductive switch dies closed by an on-card LED/VCSEL array, so a few tester channels are time-multiplexed across thousands of probe pins with optical control instead of relays.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4): tester channel count and test capex per bit fall several-fold; a small team integrates via PCB and MEMS-probe vendors.

title: Single-poly floating-gate CAM stores repair addresses without fuses
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim tunneling onto a floating gate. In a standard-logic MPW macro, repair and trim addresses live in single-poly floating-gate cells programmed through the thin gate oxide with no extra masks, arranged as a CAM that compares incoming row addresses directly. No laser fuses, no boot-time fuse broadcast, and field re-programmable for post-package repair.
why: Periphery area/yield (fact 7): fuse banks (~2% of die) removed and in-field repair raises effective yield; zero added mask cost suits a fabless team.

title: Deuterium re-passivation anneal shrinks leakage tail of reject dies
idea: Effect: hydrogen-isotope passivation of Si/SiO2 dangling bonds (Pb centers). Bare reject DRAM dies or thinned wafers are annealed in a small tube furnace in 5-10% D2 at ~350-400 C; deuterium re-passivates the traps in junction depletion regions whose SRH generation current dominates the retention tail, and the dies are re-screened before resale.
why: Refresh/yield (fact 3): if tail leakage halves, retention-fail dies become sellable and refresh can relax; furnace capex <$0.5M.

title: Biased-reference sentinel column detects disturbance before data cells flip
idea: Effect: deliberately offset sense threshold as a disturbance canary. In a small team's memory macro, each row has one sentinel cell whose sense amp uses a shifted reference (~30% of nominal signal), rewritten to 1 at every refresh; it fails before any data cell under leakage or hammer disturbance, so a flipped sentinel triggers immediate refresh of that row and its neighbors.
why: Row hammer and refresh (facts 3, 9): one cell per row (~0.1% area) replaces counter tables and acts as a built-in canary for longer default refresh.

title: Asymmetric-leakage data inversion keeps most cells in non-leaking state
idea: Effect: one-sided leakage (only charged cells decay toward error). An FPGA/CXL controller inverts each row's data whenever that leaves more cells discharged, using the module's true/anti-cell map learned once by a retention scan, and stores one inversion flag per row in spare metadata bits; zero-heavy data leaves ~70-90% of cells uncharged.
why: Refresh/reliability (fact 3): fewer charged cells means fewer retention failures, enabling ~2x longer refresh intervals at the same error rate; pure controller work.

title: Seebeck heat-flux sensors predict die temperature to drop refresh guardbands
idea: Effect: Seebeck thermopile heat-flux sensing plus package thermal lag. Laminate off-the-shelf thin-film Bi2Te3 heat-flux sensors between DRAM packages and the heat spreader; heat flux leads die temperature by tens of ms through the package's thermal RC, so the controller forecasts temperature ~50 ms ahead and runs relaxed refresh until a real rise is coming.
why: Refresh (fact 3): removing a static ~10 C guardband gives ~2x longer refresh at typical temperatures (~30-40% refresh energy) with module-level parts.

title: Stepwise tank-capacitor bitline charging cuts precharge energy several-fold
idea: Effect: adiabatic stepwise charging. In a small team's MPW macro, bitlines charge and discharge through 3-4 intermediate voltage steps supplied by on-die tank capacitors, so each step dissipates only ~C(V/N)^2; the tanks self-balance because rising and falling lines exchange charge through them.
why: Energy per bit (facts 8, 10): bitline CV^2 energy falls ~N-fold (2-3x in practice) without lowering VARY, at the cost of ~1-2 ns per step.

title: Polarity-swapping sense amps balance BTI aging to shrink offset margins
idea: Effect: bias-temperature instability (NBTI/PBTI) threshold drift. Every refresh epoch, a swap network flips which half of each SA pair connects to the true versus complement bitline (data stored inverted, one flag per mat), so BTI shifts build up equally on both transistors and cancel instead of growing into offset.
why: SA area (fact 7): reclaims the end-of-life offset margin (often ~30% of the budget), allowing smaller SA devices or longer bitlines; a pure design change on MPW.

title: Bond-wire inductive boost converter generates wordline voltage without charge pump
idea: Effect: inductive flyback (L di/dt). Use the package's existing bond-wire inductance (~1-2 nH per wire, several in parallel) as the inductor of an on-die switched boost converter at ~0.5-1 GHz, generating VPP at ~70% efficiency instead of a ~30%-efficient multi-stage capacitive pump.
why: Periphery area/energy (facts 7, 10): VPP generator area ~-60% and energy ~-50%, using only standard wire bonding and MPW CMOS.
